proof.text: The simplicial relative cone $D_0=A\amalg_{E\times\{0\}}(E\times\Delta^1)$ is a small simplicial set, since $A$ and $E$ are small; it is in general not a quasicategory (an edge $a'\to p(e)$ of $A$ followed by the cylinder edge at $e$ is an inner horn with no filler in $D_0$ unless it lifts to $E$). By [lem-coef-small-inner-horn-completion] applied to $X=D_0$, $D=RD_0$ is a small quasicategory, $D_0\to D$ is a degreewise monomorphism, and for every quasicategory $\mathcal E$ in the containing universe restriction $\operatorname{Fun}(D,\mathcal E)\to\operatorname{Fun}(D_0,\mathcal E)$ has the right lifting property against all monomorphisms. Taking $\mathcal E=\mathcal S^{\mathrm{op}}$ and opposites, restriction $\mathcal P(D)\to\mathcal P(D_0)$ is a trivial fibration, in particular an equivalence; so the mapping spaces $\operatorname{Map}_D$ and representables $y_D$ are defined, and conditions (i) and (ii), which by definition are read on the restriction $\phi|_{D_0}$, are the conditions of [lem-coef-ghn-ind-presheaf-cartesian-realization] for the presheaf $\phi|_{D_0}$ on the small simplicial set $D_0=E_A^{\triangleleft}$. That statement treats exactly this simplicial pushout with its coherent cylinder data: restriction along $j$ has fibers described by presheaves $\Psi$ on $E$ with a coherent transformation $\Psi\to p^*X$, the cocartesian-edge condition is its pullback square (i), and the fiber condition is its double-cone condition (ii). All cylinder squares and cones below are simplices of $D_0$ composed into $D$; no ordinary homotopy category is used.

source.place: Definition 9.1, Proposition 9.12 and Proposition 9.16: relative cone and presheaf fiber model

proof.text:
For every small space $Z$, the coherent slice $\mathcal S_{/Z}$ admits all small limits. Indeed [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] supplies small limits in $\mathcal S$; take opposites using [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-equivalence] and apply [lem-coef-infinity-coslice-colimit-formula] to $\mathcal S^{\mathrm{op}}$ and $Z$. Its coslice is $(\mathcal S_{/Z})^{\mathrm{op}}$. Explicitly, a diagram $Y:J\to\mathcal S$ with a coherent map to the constant $Z$ has slice limit with total space
$$Z\times_{\lim_J\Delta_J Z}\lim_JY,$$
with the cone legs supplied by that dual formula. This includes $J=\varnothing$, when both ordinary limits are points and the result is the identity $Z\to Z$. No claim that the source projection creates disconnected limits is used.

source.place: Dual of the coslice formula; HTT Section 4.4.2 and coherent mapping-space universal properties

proof.text: Fix $a$ and put $T_a:E_a^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal S_{/X(a)}$. The domain admits $\lambda$-small limits, since $E_a$ admits $\lambda$-small colimits and taking opposites exchanges these notions by [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-equivalence]. Its target admits these limits by step 2. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-limits-products-pullbacks] with $\kappa=\lambda$, $\mathcal C=E_a^{\mathrm{op}}$ and $\mathcal D=\mathcal S_{/X(a)}$. Thus (ii) is equivalent to $T_a$ taking every fiber pushout to a slice pullback and every coproduct on fewer than $\lambda$ summands to a slice product, including the empty product. This uses the bounded theorem, including its $\lambda=\aleph_0$ clause; it does not assume that $E_a$ has all small colimits.

source.place: Proposition 10.5 proof, reduction of fiber tests to pushouts and bounded coproducts

proof.text:
For a cocartesian edge $u:e\to f$ over $\alpha:a\to b$, the cylinder gives the coherent square in $D$ with initial vertex $j(a)$, adjacent vertices $j(b),e$, and final vertex $f$. Regard it as a cocone on the span $j(b)\leftarrow j(a)\to e$, with apex $f$. Applying $\phi$ reverses the arrows. The resulting comparison is exactly
$$\Psi(f)\longrightarrow X(b)\times_{X(a)}\Psi(e).$$
Its being an equivalence says exactly that the square in (i), with its specified coherence, is a pullback. These are the first family of tests; they are not asserted to be colimits in $D$.

source.place: Proposition 9.12 pullback-square condition and Proposition 10.5 first family

proof.text: Let $\bar q:K^{\triangleright}\to E_a$ be one of the pushout or coproduct cocones of step 3, with apex $c$. Restricting the cylinder gives a coherent cone from $j(a)$ to the whole diagram $\bar q$ in $D$. By the dual, fixed-apex form of [lem-coef-join-slice-cocone-comparison], using opposites from [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-equivalence], realize it as a diagram on $\Delta^0\star K\star\Delta^0$. Set $B=\Delta^0\star K$ and read this as a cocone $r:B^{\triangleright}\to D$, with initial added vertex $j(a)$ and final vertex $c$. The comparison theorem is natural under restriction of the indexing shape, so the diagram retains the prescribed fiber cocone and the cylinder compatibility, up to coherent equivalence. The equivalence invariance of limiting cones follows from the mapping-space cone criterion in [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. In particular no literal join inclusion into $D_0$ is required.

source.place: Warning 9.2, Proposition 9.16 double-cone construction; join/comma comparison

proof.text: For this cocone, $\phi r$ has apex $\Psi(c)$ and base the diagram on $(K^{\triangleleft})^{\mathrm{op}}$ consisting of $\Psi(q(k))\to X(a)$. The double-cone/slice equivalence stated in [lem-coef-ghn-ind-presheaf-cartesian-realization] says precisely that this cone is limiting if and only if $T_a$ takes $\bar q$ to a limit cone in the slice. Apply that equivalence to the restriction of $\phi$ to the simplicial cylinder $D_0$; step 5 realizes its same coherent cone in $D$. For a discrete set $I$ the comparison is the product of the arrows $\Psi(q(i))\to X(a)$ in that slice, hence the limit of their common-base star. For $I=\varnothing$ the base of $r$ is just $j(a)$ and the comparison is $\Psi(0_a)\to X(a)$. For the pushout span the comparison is the corresponding slice pullback. Together with step 3, the second family of tests is therefore equivalent to all of (ii), not just to its finite subfamily.

source.place: Proposition 9.16 coherent double-cone condition, and Proposition 10.5 fiber tests

proof.text: There is a small set of these cocones. The cocartesian edges form a subset of the small set $E_1$, and each supplies a fixed finite square. For coproducts take the discrete ordinal shapes $I=\mu$ with $\mu<\lambda$ a cardinal, including $0$; these shapes form a small set because $\lambda$ belongs to the smaller universe. For each $a$ and each such $I$, all maps $I^{\triangleright}\to E_a$ form a small set of simplicial maps; keep the colimiting ones. Do the same for the single finite pushout-span shape. Union over $a\in A_0$ is still small. Adjoining the two cone vertices leaves every test shape small (indeed $\lambda$-small). All realizations of each fixed shape in the small $D$ form a small set; choose representatives realizing the cylinder data of step 5. Relabeling any fewer-than-$\lambda$ index set by its cardinal gives an isomorphic discrete shape, and coherent equivalence of test cones preserves the limit predicate by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. Thus these representatives test every required cocone. Only universe closure under small unions, products and subsets and the definition of $\lambda$-smallness are used for the size count.

source.place: Proposition 10.5 proof, set-sized selection of cocartesian, pushout and coproduct tests

proof.text:
For every chosen $r$, apply [lem-coef-infinity-presheaf-colimit-locality] with $C=D$, $K=B_r$, the coherent cocone $r$, and $X=\phi$. Its hypotheses hold: $D$ is a small quasicategory by step 1 and $B_r$ is small by step 7. It gives the presheaf colimit and identifies precomposition with the actual map $s_r$ as
$$\phi(r(\infty))\longrightarrow\lim_{b\in B_r^{\mathrm{op}}}\phi(r(b)),$$
including its cone legs and higher coherences. Consequently locality for this $s_r$ is exactly the limit test in steps 4 and 6. The image of the small set of cocones under $r\mapsto s_r$ is a small set $S_0$. Steps 3, 4 and 6 show, in both directions, that its local objects are exactly the presheaves satisfying (i) and (ii).

source.place: Lemma 10.6 proof, representable locality maps; Proposition 10.5 conclusion about the test family

title: Small locality generators for the relative Ind presheaf conditions
statement:
Use universes, infinite regular cardinals and $\lambda$-smallness from [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category], coherent functors, spaces and limits from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and cocartesian fibrations from [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Fix an infinite regular cardinal $\lambda$ in the smaller universe. Let $A$ be a small infinity category and $F_0:A\to\operatorname{Cat}^{\mathrm{rex}(\lambda)}_\infty$ a coherent functor, where the target has small infinity categories admitting $\lambda$-small colimits as objects and functors preserving those colimits as arrows. Let $p:E\to A$ be its small cocartesian fibration, put $E_a=p^{-1}(a)$, and form the small simplicial relative cone $D_0=A\amalg_{E\times\{0\}}(E\times\Delta^1)$. Put $D=R D_0$, the small quasicategorical completion constructed in [lem-coef-small-inner-horn-completion], and use the composite maps from the cylinder into $D$, with inclusions $j:A\to D$ and $E\times\{1\}\to D$. Write $-\infty_a=j(a)$ and $\mathcal P(D)=\operatorname{Fun}(D^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S)$, with $\mathcal S$ the infinity category of small spaces and $y_D(d)=\operatorname{Map}_D(-,d)$.
For $\phi\in\mathcal P(D)$ put $X=j^*\phi$ and $\Psi=\phi|_{E\times\{1\}}$. Its cylinder data define a coherent transformation $\Psi\to p^*X$. Consider the following two conditions: (i) for every cocartesian edge $e\to\alpha_!e$ above $\alpha:a\to b$, the induced square with rows $\Psi(\alpha_!e)\to\Psi(e)$ and $X(b)\to X(a)$ is a pullback of spaces; (ii) the induced functor $E_a^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal S_{/X(a)}$ sends every $\lambda$-small colimit cocone of $E_a$ to a limit cone in the coherent slice, for every $a$.
There is a small set of coherent cocones $r:B_r^{\triangleright}\to D$, indexed by representatives of the squares in (i) and the fiber pushout and less-than-$\lambda$-indexed coproduct tests in (ii), with the common cone point included for the slice tests, such that the maps
$$s_r:\operatorname{colim}_{b\in B_r}y_D(r(b))\longrightarrow y_D(r(\infty))$$
form a small set $S_0$ whose local objects are exactly the presheaves satisfying (i) and (ii). Here $S_0$-local means that precomposition $\operatorname{Map}(y_D(r(\infty)),\phi)\to\operatorname{Map}(\operatorname{colim}_{b\in B_r}y_D(r(b)),\phi)$ is an equivalence for every $r$. Empty coproducts are included, so (ii) requires $\Psi(0_a)\to X(a)$ to be an equivalence for an initial object $0_a$ of $E_a$. All test diagrams and colimits are small relative to the smaller universe; the presheaf category is formed in a containing universe. The completion is included because the simplicial mapping-cylinder pushout need not itself be a quasicategory; all representables and test cocones here are taken in $D$, while the cylinder data are their restrictions along $D_0\to D$.
